title: Paying a Title-Delay Chargeback Shortfall — Trade-In Agreements
content:
A title-delay chargeback can leave the trade equity on a **Trade-In Agreements** agreement below zero; the customer then owes that shortfall and may pay it at once or spread it.

## Rule

When a title-delay chargeback leaves the undistributed trade equity of a picked-up trade-in agreement below zero, the customer pays the shortfall from their own funds by bank transfer within the chargeback payment days, each payment booked as one covering entry for a customer payment, dated the day it is paid, raising the undistributed trade equity by its amount. A customer who asks to spread the shortfall pays today's installment at once and the rest of the shortfall by the end of the chargeback payment days.

## Ledger entries today's installment rests on

Today's installment is fixed only after the agreement's ledger carries the title-delay chargeback owed once the title delay chargeback days have passed with no title received date.

Today's installment is not worked out until the agreement's ledger carries the towing fee deduction owed for a vehicle Kestrel collected by tow truck.

Both are read from the agreement's own history: today's installment is worked out against a ledger that already shows those entries where they are owed.

## Business effect

| Item | Effect |
|---|---|
| Agreement history | One covering entry for a customer payment per payment, dated the day it is paid |
| Undistributed trade equity | Higher by the amount paid |
| Remaining shortfall | Due by the end of the chargeback payment days |

## Customer tool reference: `pay_chargeback_shortfall_4672c84f`

**Capability.** Lets the former owner of a traded vehicle pay money of their own toward the shortfall a title-delay chargeback left on their trade-in agreement. One call makes one payment from the customer's own funds by bank transfer onto the agreement, books a covering entry of the kind `customer_payment` dated today for the amount given, and raises the agreement's undistributed trade equity by that amount; the payment shows in the agreement's history and the amount still owed drops by the amount paid.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`, naming `pay_chargeback_shortfall_4672c84f`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `trade_in_id` | Reference number of the customer's trade-in agreement, as read out to the customer by the Kestrel representative | Id |
| `payment_amount` | The amount the customer pays | USD, a positive amount to 2 decimal places, exactly as the representative quoted it |

**Return.** A text rendering of a receipt with `payment_id` (reference number of the payment), `trade_in_id` (the agreement paid on), `settlement_method` (always `customer_payment`), `amount` (USD to 2 decimal places, the amount received), `paid_on` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `equity_balance` (USD to 2 decimal places, the agreement's undistributed trade equity with the payment booked). A receipt carrying a `payment_id` means the payment is recorded.
